what_would_change_verdict: Trunk-floor and diff-mount photos or a specialist PPI showing sound structure (better still, documented reinforcement) would lift condition and documentation
Dated cooling-system and maintenance invoices plus a clean VIN history report confirming long-term single ownership would raise documentation substantially
A cheap ABS/ASC fix (e.g. a wheel-speed sensor) and a negotiated price below the fair-value mid would improve value
Down: cracked or torn trunk floor, an accident on the VIN report, a refused PPI, or an ABS module fault plus other undisclosed issues
evidence.mission_note: As a future keeper, a stock S52 manual M Roadster in a desirable colour combination is exactly the preferred configuration, and the ask is within the ideal budget band. It only meets the keeper standard once the structure, cooling history and warning lamps are documented; a $18k undocumented purchase also works against cash preservation in accelerated-bridge mode.
evidence.rationale: The photos establish identity: VIN [VIN] decodes as a 1999 BMW M car, the bay shows the S52, and the odometer reads 88,093, all matching the listing. Cosmetically the car looks tidy and stock in Titanium Silver over Estoril Blue/black, with original M wheels and exhaust. Observed wrong: the cluster photo shows the ABS and ASC lamps lit with the engine running (tach near idle, voltmeter about 14 V), which conflicts with the seller's 'All Electronics Work' and implies a stored fault. Everything model-critical remains open. There are no trunk-floor or diff-mount photos (carpet in place), no cooling records, and no service file or history report behind 'well maintained' and the near-single-owner claim. The $18,000 OBO ask sits within the $15,358-$19,599 fair-value band, slightly above the mid. The car is in Illinois, so PPI access and CA smog are logistics questions still to be answered.
